A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ResKoopNet research. Their main text, equations, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: V2 reports original pendulum simulations and comparative ResKoopNet analyses of turbulence and mouse neural recordings, including spectral, spatial-mode and clustering results.

after.justification: V3 retains original results for all three applications and reports additional dictionary-size, network-architecture and neural clustering analyses.

M1.justification: The spectral-residual objective, alternating dictionary and Koopman-matrix updates, fixed constant/coordinate functions, and pseudospectrum scan remain unchanged. Revised representation sizes are experimental configurations; minibatching and preconditioning are proposed future directions.

E1.justification: Both versions use the pendulum, the same airfoil turbulence dataset, and Sensorium recordings from five mice viewing six stimuli. Added controls and architecture sweeps retain these datasets and task requirements.

E2.justification: V3 adds mean-firing-rate features as a directly evaluated neural clustering comparator in Figures 11–12. The existing Koopman comparator sets remain: EDMD, EDMD-DL, Hankel-DMD and ResDMD for the pendulum, and Hankel-DMD, EDMD+RBF and Kernel-ResDMD for neural data.

E3.justification: The neural experiment changes from 300 SVD coordinates, 601 dictionary functions and 501 selected eigenfunctions to a reported 24 coordinates and 50 dictionary functions. Turbulence changes from 300 to 250 observables. V3 also introduces architecture sweeps. Some appendix sentences retain conflicting 300-dimensional neural preprocessing descriptions.

E4.justification: V3 adds ResDMD dictionary-size sensitivity tests, pendulum and neural network-architecture sweeps, and controls assessing whether mean firing rates already separate neural states. New singular-value plots also support analysis of the dominant turbulence mode. These substantially expand scrutiny of efficiency, robustness and interpretation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports model seeds, repeated-training uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The biological stimulus repetitions remain unchanged, and the added plots do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Figure 5 replaces turbulence results under the revised dictionary size; its leading-mode residual changes from 2.18e-8 to 8.36e-7. Figure 6 replaces the larger neural representation with 50-basis eigenfunctions and revised DBIs. Added results show reasonable ResDMD spectral recovery at 464 bases and report architecture sensitivity and mean-rate clustering. These are revised-setting and additional results, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V2's short Barron-space approximation discussion becomes an extended convergence argument in v3 Appendix A.4, adding explicit assumptions, dictionary-error bounds, a conditional expected SGD rate, and arguments connecting residual convergence to spectral convergence. Section 2 also adds a discrete/continuous Koopman decomposition. The earlier Barron theorem and residual derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The conclusion strengthens the description from mitigating spectral inclusion to successfully resolving it. The central contribution—learning dictionaries through spectral-residual minimization—and the abstract's physical/biological application claims otherwise remain essentially unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 acknowledges that mean firing rates already suffice for neural-state clustering and qualifies the ResDMD efficiency comparison using its smaller successful dictionaries. It adds an SVD-based interpretation of the leading turbulence mode, an explanation of Hankel-DMD's small-residual failures, and discussion of nonconvex convergence assumptions and computational bottlenecks.

D1.justification: V3 supplies substantially more implementation information, including exact turbulence data dimensions and sampling interval, SVD reduction/back-projection details, dictionary composition, and pendulum/neural network widths. The embedded code-access link changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository; the PDFs do not establish its operational availability.

R1.justification: V3 expands discussion of the already-cited Korda–Mezić EDMD convergence results and adds references on optimization, fluid dynamics and chaotic systems, including Bottou et al. and Schmid. The central positioning relative to ResDMD, VAMP and neural Koopman methods remains.

P1.justification: Substantial passages in the introduction, preliminaries, method explanation, physical applications and conclusion are rewritten. The pseudospectrum discussion moves into the ResDMD review, the code section moves to the appendix opening, and the appendix organization expands beyond simple renumbering.

P2.justification: Existing pendulum panels are rearranged into grids. Turbulence Figure 5 is redrawn with normalized color scales, annotations and singular-value panels, and neural Figure 6 is redrawn. New appendix figures display dictionary-size tests, architecture sweeps, raw neural activity and mean-rate comparisons; several earlier baseline figures are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: V3 improves empirical scrutiny by matching the neural dictionary count to Hankel-DMD, testing ResDMD with fewer bases, and acknowledging that simple firing-rate features can solve the neural benchmark. Additional implementation details help reproducibility. Stale preprocessing statements in A.9.4/A.10 and the gap between conditional convergence assumptions and categorical spectral-completeness claims limit the overall gain.
